newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says will defend top LNG position.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says will defend top LNG position.

text.p: The head of Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina said on Wednesday it would defend its position as the world's top liquefied natural gas (LNG) exporter despite tough international market competition.
"We will defend our position as the top LNG exporter. We will work hard for that," Pertamina president director Faisal Abda'oe told reporters.
"We plan to build Number Nine LNG train (Train I) in Bontang, because our natural gas reserves make it possible for another LNG plant there," he said.
"At the moment we are working to find a market for the gas," he added.
He said demand in the Asia-Pacific region continued to increase but competition among LNG producers was also tough.

"Demand in the Asia-Pacific region continues to increase. There is competition among LNG producers such as Qatar and Australia to feed the market. But we have several advantage such as our location, which is very close to the market," he said.
Abda'oe said Indonesia exports around 26.5 million tonnes of LNG annually, including long-term contracts, mainly to Japan, Taiwan and South Korea.
Pertamina currently has six LNG plants in Arun, Northern Sumatra's Aceh province, and another six in Bontang, East Kalimantan.
Abda'oe said Number Seven LNG plant (Train G) will soon to be completed in Bontang and construction work on Number Eight (Train H) had already begun there.
"So we believe we can defend our position as the top LNG exporter," he said.
Indonesia's Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana has said Indonesia has 115 trillion cubic feet of natural gas reserves.
